about.p1: I design the system before the screens: feature boundaries, Signals-based state, typed API contracts and shared design tokens, so large teams can move fast without breaking each other.
about.p2: Today I lead front-end architecture at Saudi Azm and migrate legacy apps to modern Angular. What drives me most is seeing a product succeed because it makes someone's day easier: filing a complaint in minutes, getting paid on time, or signing a contract from a phone.

wasl.p: A digital financing-brokerage platform, set up as a 50/50 joint venture between Saudi Azm and the National Housing Company. It connects customers with licensed financing entities across the Kingdom. The Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) granted it a digital brokerage licence in August 2026.
wasl.h1: Financing request journeys built for clarity and trust
wasl.h3: Secure, accessible Arabic-first UI to fintech standards
wasl.c: Financing is high-stakes: users must trust every step, and the platform has to meet SAMA's regulatory and security expectations from day one.
wasl.a1: Front-end architecture for request, offer and tracking flows
wasl.a2: Reusable, accessible form and status components
wasl.a3: Typed API contracts with the .NET services
wasl.r: A platform ready for full operation after the SAMA licence, on a component base that scales with new financing partners.
sba.p: A unified service for complaints against lawyers and reports against people impersonating the profession. It protects the profession's integrity and the rights of beneficiaries.

sba.h2: Quality-control queues, scoring, escalation, audit trail
sba.h3: Applicant dashboard with live case status
sba.c: Complaints carry legal weight. Every action needs an audit trail, and the UI has to work for citizens, lawyers and QC staff alike, in Arabic first.
sba.a2: QC review workflow: queues, scoring, escalation
sba.a3: Native RTL, accessible tables and forms
sba.r: A live national service that tracks each case end to end, with consistent quality review behind it.
seac.p: E-arbitration for engineering and construction disputes under the Saudi Council of Engineers, serving ministries, companies and individual engineers.
seac.h1: Portals for arbitrators, establishments, individuals and experts
seac.h2: Case filing, hearings and joining as a respondent
seac.c: Four very different user types share one case, each with its own permissions, documents and deadlines.
seac.a3: Shared component library with the other Azm platforms
seac.r: Arbitration moved online: parties file and follow cases without paper.
ct.p: Individuals and companies create, manage and e-sign contracts anytime, anywhere, with automated and auditable workflows replacing paper.
ct.h1: Separate sign-in flows for individuals and companies
ct.c: A signed contract has to be legally valid, and the experience has to work for a single person and for a large company alike.
ct.a2: Dynamic contract builder from typed schemas
ct.r: A public, self-serve e-signature product live at contracts.com.sa.

os.p: When a library breaks in production, I report it upstream with a reproducer instead of quietly working around it.
os.1: PDFs stopped rendering on iPhone 15 Pro after the 5.4 upgrade while iPhone 11 still worked. I isolated the device-specific regression.
os.2: ContextMenu items could no longer be swapped at right-click time after the processedItems internals changed.
os.3: Dialog drag broke when the cursor crossed into the body, so the handle disappeared mid-drag.
os.4: Proposed server-side lazy loading for Dropdown virtual scroll (page index and size on scroll-to-end).
